sn4.21:2.2: “Here, sir, we live not far from the Buddha, diligent, keen, and resolute.
sn4.21:2.3: Then, sir, a brahmin came up to us: with a large matted dreadlock, wearing an antelope hide, old, bent double, wheezing, and holding a staff made of cluster fig tree wood. And he said to us:
sn4.21:2.4: “You’ve gone forth while young, reverends.  With pristine black hair, you’re blessed with youth, in the prime of life, and you’ve never flirted with sensual pleasures.
sn4.21:2.6: “Don’t give up what is apparent in the present to chase after what takes effect over time.”
sn4.21:2.7: When this had been said, sir, we said to that brahmin:
sn4.21:2.8: “Brahmin, we are not giving up what is apparent in the present to chase after what takes effect over time.
sn4.21:2.9: We’re giving up what takes effect over time to chase after what is apparent in the present.
sn4.21:2.10: For the Buddha says that sensual pleasures take effect over time; they give much suffering and distress, and they are all the more full of drawbacks.
sn4.21:2.11: But this teaching is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.”
sn4.21:2.12: When this had been said, sir, that brahmin shook his head, waggled his tongue, raised his eyebrows until his brow puckered in three furrows, and left leaning on his staff.”
